events.content:
The product title now renders instantly. The page was blocking entirely on `getInventory()` — since it awaits `connection()`, the fetch is dynamic and was holding back even the static parts of the page.

I restructured `app/product/page.tsx` so the inventory fetch lives in its own async `Inventory` component wrapped in a `<Suspense>` boundary with a "Loading inventory…" fallback. With `cacheComponents` already enabled in `next.config.ts`, Next.js now prerenders the title and fallback as a static shell served immediately on navigation, and streams the stock count and price in once the live data resolves.

The build confirms it: `/product` changed to `◐ (Partial Prerender) — prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content`.
